description: Intentional error-handling patterns exempt from the error-hiding audit. Each entry uses 'function' (not 'lines') for drift-proof matching — line numbers shift on every edit, function names are stable. Each entry documents WHY the pattern is appropriate.

exclusions.reason: FileNotFoundError is expected when config file disappears between exists() check and read (TOCTOU). Falls through to return cls() which creates a safe default. This is not hiding an error — it IS the intended fallback.

ClaudeMdInjector.inject() is a strictly advisory feature — it must never crash daemon startup. Both OSError and broad Exception are caught, logged with full traceback (exc_info=exc), and swallowed so daemon continues. The return is just the early-exit path, not hiding a real error.
Returns early on ValueError for unknown event types. The caller continues normally — the footer injection is optional context enrichment, not a critical operation.
Git helper methods are explicitly non-fatal. Callers check for None and handle missing git context gracefully. These are utility methods, not critical paths.
Git helper methods are explicitly non-fatal. Callers check for None and handle missing git context gracefully. These are utility methods, not critical paths.

Catches Exception, logs full traceback via logger.exception(), returns None. Pseudo-event dispatch is non-critical — one failing pseudo-event must not crash the main hook processing pipeline. Already logged with full traceback.
Returns early when path is invalid or does not exist. Transcript reading is advisory — handlers must not crash if the transcript file is missing or the path is malformed. Callers check _loaded state.
Logs file read errors and continues with empty state. Transcript parsing is advisory — one unreadable transcript must not crash handler execution. Already logged at debug/error level.
Logs OSError/UnicodeDecodeError at debug level and returns partial results. Incremental transcript reading is advisory — same pattern as _parse(). Already logged.

JSONL transcript parsing loop: except json.JSONDecodeError: continue is the standard JSONL pattern. Malformed lines are skipped to process the rest of the transcript. Same pattern already excluded in hedging_language_detector and auto_continue_stop.

JSONL transcript tail scan for Stop-hook block markers: except json.JSONDecodeError: continue is the standard JSONL pattern. The discriminator must skip malformed lines to evaluate the rest of the lookback window — a single bad line cannot mask a genuine block marker further along. Same pattern already excluded in transcript_reader.read_incremental.

Directory search loop: log-and-continue when searching upward for .claude directory. SystemExit during path validation means invalid installation at this path — continue searching upward is the correct behaviour. Already logged at debug level.

Returns None on socket connection failure. Callers check for None and display appropriate error messages to user. Socket unavailability is a normal operational state (daemon not running). Already logged via logger.exception.
Stale socket/PID file cleanup routine: log-and-continue is correct. Cleanup failing for one stale file should not prevent cleanup of others or block daemon startup. Already logged at warning level.
Stale socket/PID file cleanup routine: log-and-continue is correct. Cleanup failing for one stale file should not prevent cleanup of others or block daemon startup. Already logged at warning level.
Returns None when PID file missing or invalid. Callers check for None before using PID. This is the documented contract — a missing PID file means no daemon is running.

Returns None when .daemon-metadata.json is missing, empty, or fails schema validation. Callers interpret None as 'treat this venv as stale and rebuild' — this IS the documented contract (Plan 00100 Phase 3). Narrow except catches only (ValidationError, ValueError) and logs at debug before returning.

Stdlib-only mirror of metadata.read_daemon_metadata (Plan 00100 Task 3.4). Returns None when .daemon-metadata.json is missing, unreadable (OSError), malformed (JSONDecodeError), or fails minimal shape checks. Callers (resolve_existing_venv_python_with_diagnostics) interpret None as 'skip this venv, fall through'. Exists separately because paths.py must stay stdlib-only — it runs under host python3 at install time, before Pydantic is installed.

Plan 00110 Phase 3 canonical discovery probe. Returns None when a glob-discovered python3.NN candidate is broken — missing exec bit, subprocess crash/hang within the bounded timeout, or unparseable version output. Callers (find_latest_python / find_latest_python_or_explain) iterate every candidate and skip None results — one broken interpreter on PATH must not abort discovery of the others.

Plan 00110 Phase 3 best-effort pyproject.toml floor reader. Returns None when the file is unreadable (OSError) — pyproject may legitimately be absent (bootstrap from fresh clone, downstream install without project pyproject). Callers fall back to the hard-coded _MIN_COMPATIBLE_PYTHON floor when None is returned. Uses regex instead of tomllib so the helper works under any host interpreter during bootstrap.
Stale socket/PID file cleanup routine: log-and-continue is correct. Cleanup failing for one stale file should not prevent cleanup of others or block daemon startup. Already logged at warning level.
Stale socket/PID file cleanup routine: log-and-continue is correct. Cleanup failing for one stale file should not prevent cleanup of others or block daemon startup. Already logged at warning level.
Stale file batch cleanup routine: log-and-continue is correct. One unremovable/unreadable file must not abort cleanup of others or block daemon startup. Already logged at warning/debug level.
Stale file batch cleanup routine: log-and-continue is correct. One unremovable/unreadable file must not abort cleanup of others or block daemon startup. Already logged at warning/debug level.
Stale file batch cleanup routine: log-and-continue is correct. One unremovable/unreadable file must not abort cleanup of others or block daemon startup. Already logged at warning/debug level.
Acceptance test collection from handlers: log-and-continue when a handler fails to provide tests. One handler failing should not prevent playbook generation from other handlers. Already logged.

psutil process iteration: except (NoSuchProcess, AccessDenied): continue is the canonical psutil pattern. Processes can disappear mid-iteration on any OS. Skipping them silently is correct — they are already gone.
Schema validator loading: returns None when schema not available. Callers check for None and skip validation or use strict mode. Schema validation is optional safety layer, not blocking.
Stale PID file check: log-and-continue when reading/parsing stale PID file. Already logged. Daemon startup should continue even if stale PID file is unreadable.

Plan 00158 dogfooding payload capture: log-and-continue on OSError (untracked dir unwritable) / RuntimeError (ProjectContext not initialised in non-daemon callers). Capture is an opt-in debug aid and must NEVER break hook dispatch, which carries safety-critical handlers. Logged at warning level, never silently swallowed. Same sanctioned fail-open contract as context_sidecar._write_sidecar and compaction_signal._write_signal.
Returns None on config load failure. Callers receive None and handle it by using defaults or raising with better context. This is the documented contract of the function.

Notification logger: logs OSError at debug level and continues. Monitoring handlers must not crash sessions because a log file is temporarily unavailable. The error is now visible in debug logs rather than silently discarded.
Transcript archiver: logs OSError at debug level and continues. Archiving is best-effort; compaction must proceed even if the archive write fails. The error is now visible in debug logs.

Plan 00135 compaction signal: logs RuntimeError (ProjectContext not initialised in unit tests / non-daemon callers) and OSError (untracked dir unwritable) at warning level and continues. Dropping the <session>.compacting marker is a best-effort observability signal for the PTY supervisor; a failed write must never block or fail a compaction. Same fail-open contract as transcript_archiver.handle and context_sidecar._write_sidecar.
Project handler acceptance test validation: log-and-continue. Acceptance test retrieval failure is non-fatal for handler loading. Already logged at warning level.
Handler module discovery: log-and-continue when a module fails to import. One broken module should not prevent other handlers from loading. Already logged at warning level.
Handler module discovery: log-and-continue when a module fails to import. One broken module should not prevent other handlers from loading. Already logged at warning level.
Session cleanup handler: logs OSError at debug level and continues. Cleanup is best-effort; session end must not be blocked by a failed temp file removal. The error is now visible in debug logs.

Hook registration checker: returns None when ProjectContext not initialized. Caller checks for None and returns empty context. Advisory handler — failure should not break session start. Already logged at debug level.

Gitignore safety checker: log-and-continue on OSError reading optional gitignore files. Advisory handler — if a gitignore file is temporarily unreadable, the check skips that file and continues. Already logged at debug level.

Gitignore safety checker: log-and-continue on OSError reading optional gitignore files. Advisory handler — if a gitignore file is temporarily unreadable, the check skips that file and continues. Already logged at debug level.

Cache reader: returns None when cache file is missing or unparseable. Caller checks for None and falls through to a fresh filesystem scan. Cache reading is advisory — failure means re-scan, not crash.

Cache writer: log-and-continue on OSError writing cache file. Cache writing is best-effort — failure means the next session re-scans instead of using cache. Advisory handler must not crash session start. Already logged at debug level.

Version check helper: returns None when cache file missing or unparseable. Caller handles None gracefully by falling through to a fresh version check. Version checking is advisory — failure should not break session start.
Version check: log-and-continue on cache write failure. Already logged. Version checking is advisory.

Version check helper: returns None when version info unavailable (subprocess failure, parse error). Callers handle None gracefully. Version checking is advisory — failure should not break session start.

Optional container confidence indicator checks: nested try/except/pass for filesystem and OS queries (uid, socket existence). These are optional scoring signals — if unavailable, skip without logging (noisy). The outer function catches and logs broader failures.

Optional container confidence indicator checks: nested try/except/pass for filesystem and OS queries (uid, socket existence). These are optional scoring signals — if unavailable, skip without logging (noisy). The outer function catches and logs broader failures.
Daemon stats handler: log-and-continue on individual stat collection failures. Status line handlers are fail-open — one stat failing must not crash the entire status line. Already logged.

Upgrade notifier reads a best-effort version-check cache file: an OSError/ValueError on read (missing/malformed JSON) means no reliable upgrade signal, so returning None (render nothing) is the correct fallback, not error hiding. Status line handlers are fail-open by design; the outer handle() also wraps this call so any other exception fails safe too.

Git branch handler: log-and-continue on subprocess failure. Status line handlers are fail-open by design — one failing element must not crash the entire status line. Already logged at debug level. (Plan 00155 T4 moved this fail-open render body out of handle() into _render_git_context() so handle() can wrap it with the render TTL cache.)
Git branch handler: log-and-continue on subprocess failure. Status line handlers are fail-open by design — one failing element must not crash the entire status line. Already logged at debug level.

Background git fetch is best-effort by design: it only refreshes remote-tracking refs so ahead/behind icons are honest. Offline hosts, missing remotes, and slow networks are expected conditions — a failed fetch must leave the status line exactly as it was (counts as stale as before), never crash or retry-storm. Already logged at debug level; the finally block still clears the in-flight marker.

Model context effort level reader: log-and-continue on settings file read failure (OSError, invalid JSON). Status line handlers are fail-open by design — settings stays empty and falls through to daemon default. Already logged at warning level.

Startup cleanup status handler: log-and-continue on OSError reading cleanup_status.json. Status line handlers are fail-open by design — one failing element must not crash the entire status line. Returns empty context on error. Already logged at debug level.

Plan 00135 observe-only context sidecar: log-and-continue on RuntimeError (ProjectContext not initialised in unit tests / non-daemon callers) and OSError (untracked dir unwritable). Status line handlers are fail-open by design — a failed best-effort sidecar write must never crash the render or the dispatch. The sidecar is an advisory sensor for the PTY supervisor, not a critical path. Both errors are logged at warning level, never silently swallowed. Same fail-open contract as notification_logger.handle and startup_cleanup.handle.
Stats cache reader: returns None when cache file missing or unparseable. Status line callers handle None by omitting the stats section. Status line must never crash the terminal display.

Supervisor indicator /proc scan: returns None when /proc is unreadable (OSError). An unreadable /proc means the supervisor cannot be discovered by process, so the caller falls back to the status-file presence check. Status line handlers are fail-open by design — a scan failure must never crash the render. Already logged at debug level.

Supervisor indicator status-file reader: returns None when the status file is missing or unparseable (OSError/ValueError). The caller treats None as 'no usable status pid' and falls back to the /proc scan. Status line handlers are fail-open by design; the status file is best-effort. Already logged at debug level.

Supervisor indicator cmdline reader: returns None when /proc/{pid}/cmdline is unreadable (process gone between listing and read, or permission). None means the pid is not confirmable as the supervisor, so the caller skips it. Status line handlers are fail-open by design. Already logged at debug level.

_log_stop_event(): Non-critical JSONL append — logs at debug level and continues when ProjectContext is not initialised (unit tests) or the log file is unwritable. Stop event logging is purely diagnostic and must not affect the handler decision or raise to callers.

JSONL transcript parsing loop: except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError): continue is the standard JSONL pattern. Malformed lines are skipped to process the rest of the transcript. Logging each malformed line would be excessively noisy.

Subagent completion logger: logs OSError at debug level and continues. Monitoring handlers must not crash sessions because a log file is temporarily unavailable. The error is now visible in debug logs rather than silently discarded.

Process management during installation: nested try/except/pass for OS signal operations (kill, SIGTERM, SIGKILL). Inner exceptions (ProcessLookupError) indicate the process already died — a success condition. Outer try handles unexpected signal failures gracefully.
Plugin loader: returns None when plugin import or instantiation fails. Logged at error level before returning. The plugin system is resilient — one broken plugin does not prevent others from loading.
Plugin acceptance test validation: log-and-continue. Acceptance test retrieval failure is non-fatal for plugin loading. Already logged at warning level.
save_results(): Returns None when JSON result file cannot be written. Prints error to stdout. QA result saving is an auxiliary function — failure does not affect QA pass/fail determination.

Optional container confidence indicator checks: nested try/except/pass for filesystem and OS queries (uid, socket existence, project root). These are optional scoring signals — if unavailable, skip without logging (noisy). The outer function catches and logs broader failures.

Optional container confidence indicator checks: nested try/except/pass for filesystem and OS queries (uid, socket existence, project root). These are optional scoring signals — if unavailable, skip without logging (noisy). The outer function catches and logs broader failures.

Bounded git subprocess wrapper for GitRepo: returns None when git is unavailable (OSError/SubprocessError) or the command exits non-zero (e.g. not a git repo, config key absent). Same explicitly-non-fatal contract as project_context._get_git_toplevel — 'not a repo' / 'key absent' IS the answer, consumed as feature-detection by resolve_for/read_config.

Returns None when the per-repo plan counter is unset or non-integer (corrupt). None is the documented 'no counter yet' signal that triggers bootstrap-from-scan in next_plan_number_for_target — it is the intended control-flow path, not a swallowed error.

Advisory handler: a git-config counter-write failure must not block plan creation. Logs the failure with a full traceback (exc_info=True) and continues — the next read re-bootstraps the counter from a filesystem scan, so the counter self-heals rather than going silently stale. Same sanctioned pattern as transcript_reader._parse.

JSONL state-file parsing loop (Plan 00142): except json.JSONDecodeError: continue is the standard JSONL pattern — identical to transcript_reader.read_incremental and hedging_language_detector._parse_transcript. The best-effort background-process state file may contain a corrupt or partial final line; one bad line must not abort reading the remaining tracked pgids.

Returns None when ProjectContext is not initialised (unit tests, or any non-daemon caller). The caller skips the best-effort state-file write when None — the rate-limited advisory is the primary function and must never crash a tool call. Same explicitly-non-fatal contract as hook_registration_checker._get_project_root (Plan 00142).

Plan 00143: persisting project-handler load failures is observability ONLY — it must never crash handler loading / daemon startup. Catches RuntimeError (e.g. ProjectContext not initialised in non-daemon callers / unit tests), logs a visible warning, and continues. The degraded-protection signal is a safety net, not a critical path; same explicitly-non-fatal contract as background_process_tracker._resolve_state_file.

Plan 00143: best-effort write of the project-handler load-failure state file under the daemon untracked dir. A filesystem error (OSError) must not crash daemon startup — logged at warning level and skipped. Same fail-open contract as the daemon/paths.py cleanup writers and gitignore_safety_checker._write_cache.

Plan 00143: best-effort removal of the project-handler load-failure state file (clears stale degraded state when the daemon now loads cleanly). An OSError unlinking the file must not crash daemon startup — logged at warning level and skipped. Same fail-open cleanup contract as daemon/paths.py cleanup_socket / cleanup_pid_file.

Best-effort self-heal of the echd-capture helper's executable bit (e.g. a client checkout with git core.fileMode=false). A chmod OSError is logged at warning level, never swallowed, and the resolver degrades to returning None so the caller falls back to the temp-file guidance rather than crashing a pipe-block message. Same fail-open contract as handlers/status_line/context_sidecar.py — recommending a capture helper is advisory, never a critical path.
